_doc: AUTHORED contract overlay for kit parts (ADR-043). Merged over the GENERATED manifest assets/.../kit/firebase_set.json by KitRegistry. Authored, never generated: this is the CollisionTable precedent, where a naming heuristic once shipped barracks_bunker.glb as SOFT COVER because its name contained 'rack' - a bunker you could shoot through. Author the entry; do not name your way into a material.
_why_this_file_exists: A kit part cannot use the monolith's mechanism. Destruction there matches the MESH name against FSB_STRUCTURE_KINDS, which works because gen_firebase.py stamped instances named fb_bunker_fighting_i*. The standalone kit GLBs were exported in July as a REVIEW artefact and their visible meshes carry Blender workbench names - fb_bunker_fighting.glb's mesh is 'WB_bunker_rifle' while its collider is 'fb_bunker_fighting_000-colonly'. That is FAILURE MODE 3 of the destructible-export skill exactly: ballistics reads the COLLIDER name, destruction reads the MESH name, and divergence gives you half a system that looks like it works. A stamped part knows its own id, so the kit resolves identity from DATA instead of inferring it from a name.

_fields.destructible: Destructible.HP_FOR kind, or "" for a DELIBERATE ruling that this part is not a structure. Never absent - an absent entry fails the stamp loudly, which is the point.
_fields.structure_meshes: Exact visible mesh names that ARE the structure. Explicit, never a prefix guess: fb_bunker_mg.glb also contains m60.002 and m60_pintle, and a machine gun is not a bunker.
_fields.soft: true = soft_cover (round passes at 0.8x, concealment). false = hard_surface. Earth, sandbag and timber are hard, and that is deliberate.
_fields.note: Why, when the answer is not obvious.

fb_bunker_mg.note: m60.002 and m60_pintle are the gun on top of it, deliberately excluded - destroying the bunker must not require destroying the weapon as a separate structure.

fb_gate_assembly.note: DELIBERATE, and it is a P3 item rather than a ruling. This July review export is five loose meshes - watchtower_1.001, gate_left/right, gate_post_left/right - with NO colliders and a Blender .001 suffix. It is the gate house he asked to be rebuilt; give it a kind when the rebuilt part lands, not before.

fb_emplacement_m101.note: DELIBERATE. Not a structure: it is the howitzer, its ammunition and its baked crew rigs (119 meshes). The firebase swaps this chunk in over its own baked emplacement via SitePlanner._wire_m101_rigs; it is not something a sapper blows down.
